items.prompt:
Saying the same idea twice is:
A) redundant
B) precise
C) concise

Using too many unnecessary words is being:
A) wordy
B) concise
C) precise

Which is more concise for 'due to the fact that'?
A) because
B) on account of the reason that
C) owing to the fact

Which is the MOST concise?
A) 'We stayed in because it rained.'
B) 'Due to the fact that it was raining, we made the decision to stay inside.'
C) 'On account of the rain that was falling, we stayed in.'
items.answer: A) 'We stayed in because it rained.'

solution.answer: A) 'We stayed in because it rained.'

items.prompt:
Which phrase is REDUNDANT?
A) 'the two twins'
B) 'the twins'
C) 'both children'

steps: 'Twins' already means two. Key is A.

items.prompt:
Which is the most PRECISE?
A) 'She hurried to the door.'
B) 'She went quickly to the door in a fast way.'
C) 'She moved to the door fast.'

Which sentence is both concise AND correct?
A) 'The unique design impressed the judges.'
B) 'The very unique design impressed the judges.'
C) 'The really very unique design impressed the judges.'
items.answer: A) 'The unique design impressed the judges.'

solution.answer: A) 'The unique design impressed the judges.'

items.prompt:
Which revision BEST removes wordiness from 'At this point in time, we are currently in the process of planning'?
A) 'We are planning now.'
B) 'At the current time, we are now planning.'
C) 'We are in the process of currently planning at this time.'

steps: Cuts all redundancy. Key is A.
